lessons.title: Lo conosco
lessons.outcome: Replace a known person or thing with lo, la, li, le, and use mi, ti, ci, vi inside the sentence.

activities.body: When you both know what you are talking about, a short pronoun replaces it and goes right before the verb: lo (him, it), la (her, it), li (them, masculine), le (them, feminine). For the people in the conversation: mi, ti, ci, vi.

examples.it: Marco? Lo conosco bene.
examples.en: Marco? I know him well.

examples.it: La pizza? La mangio stasera.
examples.en: The pizza? I'm eating it tonight.

examples.it: I libri? Li leggo in treno.
examples.en: The books? I read them on the train.

examples.it: Le chiavi? Le vedo, sono qui.
examples.en: The keys? I see them, they're here.

examples.it: Mi chiami domani?
examples.en: Will you call me tomorrow?

examples.it: Voglio vederlo domani.
examples.en: I want to see him tomorrow.

activities.tip: Before a vowel or h, lo and la become l': l'aspetto, l'ho visto. After volere, dovere or potere, the pronoun can attach to the end of the infinitive instead: vederlo, chiamarla.

activities.en: The present? I'm buying it tomorrow.
activities.explanation: Il regalo is masculine singular, so it becomes lo, placed right before compro.
activities.hint: Name the thing first, then replace it.

activities.en: The keys? I can't find them!

blanks.explanation: Le chiavi is feminine plural: le.

activities.hint: Look at the gender and number of le chiavi.

activities.template: Il caffè ____ prendo al bar, la pizza ____ mangio a casa.
activities.en: Coffee I have at the bar, pizza I eat at home.

blanks.explanation: Il caffè is masculine singular: lo.
La pizza is feminine singular: la.

activities.hint: Each pronoun matches the thing just named.

activities.en: I have to call her before dinner.
activities.explanation: After dovere, the pronoun attaches to the end of the infinitive: chiamarla (her).
activities.hint: The pronoun hides at the end of a verb.

activities.en: The film? I'm watching it tonight.

blanks.explanation: Io takes -o: guardo or vedo.

sourceExamples.en: The film? I am watching it tonight.
sourceExamples.sourceNote: Lo refers to the masculine noun il film; it does not describe the speaker’s gender.

activities.hint: Who is doing it? Io.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Ciao! Hai visto Marco oggi?
turns.en: Hi! Have you seen Marco today?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: No, but I'll call ____ tonight.

blanks.explanation: Marco is one man: lo.

reactions.it: Perfetto! Allora ci vediamo tutti sabato.
reactions.en: Perfect! Then we'll all see each other on Saturday.
All right, we'll talk later.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Sabato c'è la festa di Anna. Vieni?
turns.en: On Saturday there's Anna's party. Are you coming?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Sure! Will you ____ in front of the bar?

blanks.explanation: Tu takes -i: aspetti (wait for me), chiami (call me).

sourceExamples.en: Sure! Will you wait for me in front of the café?
sourceExamples.it: Certo! Mi aspetti davanti al bar?

reactions.en: Of course, I'll wait for you at eight.
Yes, I'll call you when I arrive.

reactions.it: Va bene, allora ci vediamo lì alle otto.
reactions.en: All right, then see you there at eight.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: A sabato!
turns.en: See you Saturday!

activities.en: Anna? I've been waiting for her here for ten minutes.

blanks.explanation: Anna is one woman, so la; before a vowel la becomes l': l'aspetto.

activities.hint: Aspetto starts with a vowel.
Pick who, then a pronoun + verb, then when or where.
examples: Anche io li aspetto al bar volentieri.

lessons.title: Chi, che cosa, perché
lessons.outcome: Ask with chi, che cosa, dove, quando, come, quanto and perché, and answer a perché question with perché.

activities.body: A question word opens the question and the verb comes right after it. Perché means why in the question and because in the answer.

examples.it: Chi è quella ragazza?
examples.en: Who is that girl?

examples.it: Che cosa fai stasera?
examples.en: What are you doing tonight?

examples.it: Dove abita tuo fratello?
examples.en: Where does your brother live?

examples.it: Quando parte il treno?
examples.en: When does the train leave?

examples.it: Quanto costa questo libro?
examples.en: How much does this book cost?

examples.it: Perché studi l'italiano? Perché mi piace.
examples.en: Why do you study Italian? Because I like it.

activities.tip: Che cosa, cosa and che all mean what: Che cosa fai? Cosa fai? Che fai? Quale agrees in number (quale libro, quali libri) and quanto agrees like an adjective before a noun (quanti anni, quante ore).

activities.en: Who is coming to the party tonight?
activities.explanation: Chi takes a singular verb: chi viene.
activities.hint: Start with the question word.

activities.template: ____ abiti? Abito a Bologna, ____ lavoro lì.
activities.en: Where do you live? I live in Bologna, because I work there.

blanks.explanation: To ask about a place: dove.
The reason follows the main idea: perché (because).

activities.hint: The answer names a city.

activities.template: Che cosa ____ domenica? Vado al mare.
activities.en: What are you doing on Sunday? I'm going to the seaside.

blanks.explanation: The answer says vado, so the question is to tu: fai.

sourceExamples.en: What are you doing on Sunday? I am going to the seaside.
sourceExamples.it: Che cosa fai domenica? Vado al mare.

activities.hint: Who answers? Io, so the question is to tu.

activities.en: Why are you tired? Because I work too much.
activities.answer: Perché sei stanco? Perché lavoro troppo.
activities.explanation: Perché opens both the question (why) and the answer (because).
activities.hint: The same word starts both sentences.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Ciao! Sabato faccio una festa a casa mia.
turns.en: Hi! On Saturday I'm having a party at my place.

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Great! ____ does it start?

blanks.explanation: To ask about the time: a che ora or quando.

reactions.it: Alle nove, ma puoi arrivare anche prima.
reactions.en: At nine, but you can come earlier too.
Saturday evening, around nine.
At nine, at my place.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Viene anche Sara con il suo ragazzo.
turns.en: Sara is coming too, with her boyfriend.

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Really? ____ is her boyfriend?

blanks.explanation: Asking about a person: chi.

reactions.it: Si chiama Paolo, è di Napoli. Lo conosci?
reactions.en: His name is Paolo, he's from Naples. Do you know him?
His name is Paolo. Do you know him?

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Allora vieni? Porta qualcosa da bere!
turns.en: So, are you coming? Bring something to drink!

turns.speaker: you
turns.template: Certo che vengo! Perché non invitiamo anche ____?
turns.en: Of course I'm coming! Why don't we invite ____ too?

blanks.explanation: Any name works: the question is perché non + verb.

reactions.en: Good idea, I'll call him right away.
Good idea, I'll call her right away.
Good idea!

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Perfetto, a sabato!
turns.en: Perfect, see you Saturday!

activities.template: ____ libro preferisci? Questo. E ____ anni hai? Trenta.
activities.en: Which book do you prefer? This one. And how old are you? Thirty.

blanks.explanation: One book: quale (singular).
Gli anni are masculine plural: quanti anni.

activities.hint: Both words agree with the noun that follows.
Pick who, a verb, what, then the reason with perché.
examples: Io studio l'italiano perché è utile.
Noi leggiamo il giornale perché è interessante.

lessons.title: Quindi, allora, però
lessons.outcome: Join two ideas with quindi, allora, però, invece, anche, infatti, perché and poiché.

activities.body: One short word joins two ideas and says how they are linked: quindi and allora give the result, però and invece a contrast, perché and poiché the reason, infatti a confirmation, and anche adds something.

examples.it: Piove, quindi resto a casa.
examples.en: It's raining, so I'm staying at home.

examples.it: Sei stanco? Allora riposati un po'.
examples.en: Are you tired? Then rest a little.

examples.it: Mi piace il mare, però preferisco la montagna.
examples.en: I like the sea, but I prefer the mountains.

examples.it: Lui beve il caffè, io invece prendo il tè.
examples.en: He drinks coffee; I have tea instead.

examples.it: Non esco perché sono stanco.
examples.en: I'm not going out because I'm tired.

examples.it: Poiché è tardi, andiamo a casa.
examples.en: Since it's late, let's go home.

examples.it: Fa freddo, infatti nevica.
examples.en: It's cold; in fact, it's snowing.

activities.tip: Perché gives the reason after the main idea; poiché can open the sentence. Allora often opens a reply: Allora, andiamo? Anche goes right before the word it adds: anche io, anche stasera.

activities.en: Today it's raining, so I'm taking the umbrella.
activities.explanation: The rain is the reason and the umbrella is the result: quindi.
activities.hint: Which word gives a result?

activities.template: Ho fame, ____ mangio un panino. Non ho sete, ____ bevo un po' d'acqua.
activities.en: I'm hungry, so I'm eating a sandwich. I'm not thirsty, but I'm drinking a little water.

blanks.explanation: Hunger leads to the sandwich: quindi or allora.
No thirst, yet some water: a contrast, però.

activities.hint: Does the second idea follow from the first, or go against it?

activities.template: Sono stanco, quindi stasera ____ a casa.
activities.en: I'm tired, so tonight I'm staying at home.

blanks.explanation: Io takes -o: resto, rimango.

sourceExamples.en: I am tired, so tonight I am staying at home.
sourceExamples.sourceNote: The current fixed template explicitly quotes a masculine speaker (stanco). Resto itself is invariant for speaker gender; this is not a feminine learner’s own sentence. The feminine context remains unavailable until an explicit quote label or a current template remedy is provided.
sourceExamples.it: Sono stanco, quindi stasera resto a casa.

activities.hint: Who is tired? Io.

activities.en: Since it's late, we're going back home.
activities.answer: Poiché è tardi, torniamo a casa.
activities.explanation: Poiché can open the sentence; perché normally follows the main idea.
activities.hint: Which reason word can start a sentence?

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Ciao! Prendi un caffè con me?
turns.en: Hi! Will you have a coffee with me?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Gladly, ____ I only have ten minutes.

blanks.explanation: A contrast: però or ma.

reactions.it: Va bene, allora facciamo in fretta!
reactions.en: All right, then let's be quick!

reactions.it: Va bene, allora un caffè veloce.
reactions.en: All right, then a quick coffee.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Perché hai così poco tempo?
turns.en: Why do you have so little time?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Because at three I have ____.

blanks.explanation: Perché + the reason: ho una lezione.

sourceExamples.en: Because at three I have a lesson.
sourceExamples.it: Perché alle tre ho una lezione.

reactions.en: Are you still studying? What do you study?
I see, then a quick coffee.

reactions.it: Al lavoro? Allora andiamo subito al bar.
reactions.en: At work? Then let's go to the bar right away.

reactions.it: Capisco. Allora solo un caffè veloce.
reactions.en: I see. Then just a quick coffee.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Lo prendi con lo zucchero?
turns.en: Do you take it with sugar?

turns.speaker: you
turns.template: No, lo prendo amaro, ____ non mi piace lo zucchero.
turns.en: No, I take it without sugar, ____ I don't like sugar.

blanks.explanation: The reason follows: perché.

reactions.it: Anche io! Allora due caffè amari.
reactions.en: Me too! Then two black coffees.
All right, two coffees.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Due caffè, per favore!
turns.en: Two coffees, please!

activities.template: Marco studia medicina, sua sorella ____ studia legge. Io studio il tedesco e ____ il francese.
activities.en: Marco studies medicine; his sister, instead, studies law. I study German and also French.

blanks.explanation: A contrast between two people: invece.
Adding one more thing: anche.

activities.hint: One word contrasts, the other adds.
Who, what they do, what, then a connector.
examples: Io guardo un film perché piove.
Noi cuciniamo la pasta anche stasera.

lessons.title: La mia giornata
lessons.outcome: Tell your daily routine with reflexive verbs in the present, and say when you got up with the passato prossimo.

activities.body: A reflexive verb comes with a pronoun that matches the subject: mi, ti, si, ci, vi, si. The pronoun goes before the verb. In the passato prossimo the verb takes essere and the participle agrees with the subject.

examples.it: Mi sveglio alle sette.
examples.en: I wake up at seven.

examples.it: Ti alzi presto la mattina?
examples.en: Do you get up early in the morning?

examples.it: Marco si lava e si veste in dieci minuti.
examples.en: Marco washes and gets dressed in ten minutes.

examples.it: Ci vediamo alle otto davanti al bar.
examples.en: We'll see each other at eight in front of the bar.

examples.it: Ieri mi sono alzato tardi.
examples.en: Yesterday I got up late.

examples.it: Vi divertite al mare?
examples.en: Are you having fun at the seaside?

activities.tip: The infinitive ends in -si: alzarsi, svegliarsi. In the passato prossimo use essere and make the participle agree: mi sono alzato (a man), mi sono alzata (a woman), ci siamo alzati.

activities.en: In the morning I wake up at seven.
activities.answer: La mattina mi sveglio alle sette.
accepted: Mi sveglio alle sette la mattina.
activities.hint: The pronoun matches io.

activities.template: Mia sorella ____ presto, poi ____ in fretta.
activities.en: My sister gets up early, then she gets dressed in a hurry.

blanks.explanation: Mia sorella is lei: si alza.
Lei: si veste.

activities.hint: Lei takes si and the -a / -e ending.

activities.en: In the evening I ____ around eleven.

blanks.explanation: Io: mi addormento.

sourceExamples.en: In the evening I fall asleep around eleven.
sourceExamples.it: La sera mi addormento verso le undici.

activities.hint: Pronoun and ending both match io.

activities.en: Yesterday Anna got up very late.
activities.answer: Ieri Anna si è alzata molto tardi.
activities.explanation: Reflexive verbs take essere, and the participle agrees with Anna: alzata.
activities.hint: Which auxiliary do reflexive verbs take?

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: A che ora ti svegli di solito?
turns.en: What time do you usually wake up?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Usually I ____ at seven.

blanks.explanation: Io: mi sveglio, mi alzo.

sourceExamples.en: I usually wake up at seven.
sourceExamples.it: Di solito mi sveglio alle sette.

reactions.it: Presto! E poi che cosa fai?
reactions.en: Early! And then what do you do?

reactions.it: Alle sette? Io mi alzo alle otto. E poi?
reactions.en: At seven? I get up at eight. And then?

reactions.it: Capisco. E poi che cosa fai?
reactions.en: I see. And then what do you do?

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Fai colazione a casa o al bar?
turns.en: Do you have breakfast at home or at the bar?

turns.speaker: you
turns.template: Faccio colazione ____, poi mi lavo e mi vesto.
turns.en: I have breakfast ____, then I wash and get dressed.

blanks.explanation: Either answer works: a casa or al bar.

reactions.it: Anche io, un caffè veloce e poi esco.
reactions.en: Me too, a quick coffee and then I go out.
How nice, with a croissant?
Good. And in the evening?

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: E la sera, a che ora vai a letto?
turns.en: And in the evening, what time do you go to bed?

turns.speaker: you
turns.template: Vado a letto alle undici, ma ____ subito.
turns.en: I go to bed at eleven, but I ____ right away.

blanks.explanation: Io: mi addormento.

sourceExamples.en: I go to bed at eleven, but I fall asleep right away.
sourceExamples.it: Vado a letto alle undici, ma mi addormento subito.

reactions.it: Che fortuna! Io non dormo mai bene.
reactions.en: Lucky you! I never sleep well.
Really? I, instead, sleep badly.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Allora ci vediamo domani alle otto!
turns.en: Then see you tomorrow at eight!

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: All right, ____!

blanks.explanation: Ci vediamo: we'll see each other.

reactions.en: See you tomorrow, good night!
Good night!

activities.template: Stamattina Marco e Luca ____ alzati presto e ____ fatto colazione insieme.
activities.en: This morning Marco and Luca got up early and had breakfast together.

blanks.explanation: Alzarsi takes essere: si sono alzati.
Fare takes avere: hanno fatto.

activities.hint: Reflexive verbs take essere; fare takes avere.
Who, a reflexive verb, when, and where if you like.
examples: Io mi alzo alle sette la mattina.
I bambini si divertono molto al mare.

lessons.title: Più o meno
lessons.outcome: Compare people and things with più … di, meno … di, come and il più …, with the adjective agreeing.

activities.prompt: What + is + più / meno + adjective + di + what
activities.body: To compare, put più (more) or meno (less) before the adjective and di before the second term. Come says as … as. Il più / la più + adjective makes the superlative. The adjective agrees with the thing you describe.

examples.it: Il treno è più veloce dell'autobus.
examples.en: The train is faster than the bus.

examples.it: La bici è meno cara della macchina.
examples.en: The bike is less expensive than the car.

examples.it: Marco è alto come Luca.
examples.en: Marco is as tall as Luca.

examples.it: Queste scarpe sono più comode di quelle.
examples.en: These shoes are more comfortable than those.

examples.it: Anna è la più giovane della famiglia.
examples.en: Anna is the youngest in the family.

examples.it: Questo caffè è il migliore della città.
examples.en: This coffee is the best in the city.

activities.tip: Di joins the article: di + il = del, di + la = della, di + l' = dell'. Buono has its own comparative, migliore (better), and the superlative is il migliore (the best).

activities.en: The train is faster than the car.
activities.answer: Il treno è più veloce della macchina.
activities.explanation: Di + la = della; veloce agrees with il treno (singular).
activities.hint: Più + adjective + di.

activities.template: Queste scarpe sono più ____ di quelle, ma anche più ____.
activities.en: These shoes are more comfortable than those, but also more expensive.

blanks.explanation: Le scarpe is feminine plural: comode.
Feminine plural: care.

activities.hint: Le scarpe: feminine, plural.

activities.template: Mio fratello è più ____ di me.
activities.en: My brother is more ____ than me.

blanks.explanation: Mio fratello is masculine singular: alto, giovane, simpatico.

sourceExamples.en: My brother is taller than I am.
sourceExamples.sourceNote: Alto agrees with mio fratello, not with the speaker.
sourceExamples.it: Mio fratello è più alto di me.

activities.hint: Any adjective that fits a man.

activities.en: Anna is the youngest in the family.
activities.answer: Anna è la più giovane della famiglia.
activities.explanation: Anna is feminine: la più giovane; di + la famiglia = della famiglia.
activities.hint: Article + più + adjective.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Domenica andiamo a Firenze. Prendiamo il treno o la macchina?
turns.en: On Sunday we're going to Florence. Shall we take the train or the car?

turns.speaker: you
turns.template: Il treno! È più ____ della macchina.
turns.en: The train! It's more ____ than the car.

blanks.explanation: Il treno is masculine singular: veloce, comodo, economico.

sourceExamples.en: The train! It is more comfortable than the car.
sourceExamples.sourceNote: Comodo agrees with il treno, independent of the speaker’s gender.
sourceExamples.it: Il treno! È più comodo della macchina.

reactions.it: È vero, in un'ora siamo lì.
reactions.en: True, in an hour we're there.

reactions.it: Sì, e il biglietto costa meno del parcheggio.
reactions.en: Yes, and the ticket costs less than the parking.

reactions.it: Giusto, e possiamo leggere in viaggio.
reactions.en: Right, and we can read on the way.
You're right, let's take the train.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: E dove mangiamo? Conosco una pizzeria piccola ma molto buona.
turns.en: And where do we eat? I know a small but very good pizzeria.

turns.speaker: you
turns.template: Perfetto! Una pizzeria è meno ____ di un ristorante.
turns.en: Perfect! A pizzeria is less ____ than a restaurant.

blanks.explanation: Una pizzeria is feminine singular: cara, costosa.

sourceExamples.en: Perfect! A pizzeria is less expensive than a restaurant.
sourceExamples.sourceNote: Costosa agrees with una pizzeria, independent of the speaker’s gender.
sourceExamples.it: Perfetto! Una pizzeria è meno costosa di un ristorante.

reactions.en: Exactly, and the food is good.
True. Then it's settled!

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Allora treno alle nove e pranzo in pizzeria. È il piano migliore!
turns.en: So, train at nine and lunch at the pizzeria. It's the best plan!

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Yes! Florence is ____ city in Italy.

blanks.explanation: Città is feminine: la più bella.

reactions.en: I agree! I can't wait.
Then see you Sunday!

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: A domenica alle nove!
turns.en: See you Sunday at nine!

activities.template: Questo caffè è buono ____ quello del bar. Anzi, è il ____ della città!
activities.en: This coffee is as good as the one from the bar. Actually, it's the best in the city!

blanks.explanation: As … as: buono come.
The best: il migliore (or il più buono).

activities.hint: Equal first, then the top.
Everything here is masculine singular, so the adjective keeps its -o or -e.
examples: Il treno è più veloce della macchina.
Il mio telefono sembra più grande del tuo.

lessons.title: Una vera chiacchierata
lessons.outcome: Hold a longer conversation: replace with a pronoun, ask, join ideas, tell your day and compare.

activities.body: A real chat mixes everything: a pronoun instead of a repeated noun, a question word, a connector, a reflexive verb and a comparison, in the present and in the past.

examples.it: Ieri mi sono svegliato tardi, quindi ho perso il treno.
examples.en: Yesterday I woke up late, so I missed the train.

examples.it: Il film? L'ho visto, però non mi è piaciuto.
examples.en: The film? I saw it, but I didn't like it.

examples.it: Perché non vieni? Perché domani mi alzo presto.
examples.en: Why aren't you coming? Because tomorrow I'm getting up early.

examples.it: Questa pizza è più buona di quella di ieri.
examples.en: This pizza is better than yesterday's.

activities.tip: L'ho visto: before ho, lo becomes l'. With la the participle agrees: la pizza? L'ho mangiata.

activities.en: The film? I saw it last night.
activities.answer: Il film? L'ho visto ieri sera.
activities.explanation: Before ho, lo becomes l': l'ho visto. Il film is masculine: visto.
activities.hint: The pronoun and ho join into one word.

activities.template: Stamattina ____ sono alzata presto, ____ ho perso l'autobus.
activities.en: This morning I (f) got up early, but I missed the bus.

blanks.explanation: Io: mi sono alzata.
Up early, yet late: a contrast, però or ma.

activities.hint: A reflexive in the past, then a contrast.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Ciao! Non ti vedo da un mese. Come stai?
turns.en: Hi! I haven't seen you for a month. How are you?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Fine, thanks! But ____.

blanks.explanation: Sono + an adjective that agrees with you, or ho + sonno / fame.

sourceExamples.en: Fine, thanks! But I am tired.
Fine, thanks! But I am tired.
Fine, thanks! But I am sleepy.
sourceExamples.sourceNote: Ho sonno is an accepted whole phrase; it is not an adjective after sono.

reactions.it: Perché? Che cosa hai fatto ieri?
reactions.en: Why? What did you do yesterday?
Sleepy? Did you sleep little?

reactions.it: Capisco. Che cosa hai fatto ieri?
reactions.en: I see. What did you do yesterday?

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Dai, racconta! Com'è andata la giornata?
turns.en: Come on, tell me! How did your day go?

turns.speaker: you
turns.template: Ieri ____ alle sei e ho lavorato tutto il giorno.
turns.en: Yesterday I ____ at six and worked all day.

blanks.explanation: A reflexive in the past: mi sono + a participle that agrees with you.

reactions.it: Alle sei? Io mi alzo sempre alle otto.
reactions.en: At six? I always get up at eight.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: E stasera? Vieni al cinema con noi?
turns.en: And tonight? Are you coming to the cinema with us?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Gladly! ____ film are you seeing?

blanks.explanation: Which film: quale (or che) film.

reactions.en: An Italian comedy, a new one.
An Italian comedy.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Per me è più divertente di quella dell'anno scorso.
turns.en: For me it's funnier than last year's.

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Perfect, then I'll ____ with you.

blanks.explanation: Io: vengo; or a pronoun + verb: lo vedo (il film), la vedo (la commedia).

sourceExamples.en: Perfect, then I will come with you.

reactions.it: Benissimo! Ci vediamo alle otto davanti al cinema.
reactions.en: Great! See you at eight in front of the cinema.

reactions.en: Good! Then see you at eight in front of the cinema.

reactions.en: Perfect! At eight in front of the cinema.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Il cinema è lontano. Prendiamo l'autobus o andiamo a piedi?
turns.en: The cinema is far. Shall we take the bus or walk?

turns.speaker: you
turns.template: A piedi! È più ____ e non costa niente.
turns.en: On foot! It's more ____ and it costs nothing.

blanks.explanation: Più + a masculine singular adjective: bello, sano, comodo.

sourceExamples.en: On foot! It is more convenient and costs nothing.
sourceExamples.it: A piedi! È più comodo e non costa niente.

reactions.it: Hai ragione, e stasera non piove. A stasera!
reactions.en: You're right, and tonight it isn't raining. See you tonight!

reactions.it: D'accordo, allora andiamo a piedi. A stasera!
reactions.en: All right, then we'll walk. See you tonight!

activities.template: Il nuovo film ____ più divertente del vecchio? Sì, ____ consiglio!
activities.en: Is the new film funnier than the old one? Yes, I recommend it!

blanks.explanation: Il film is singular: è.
Il film is masculine singular: lo consiglio (te lo consiglio: I recommend it to you).

activities.hint: Singular verb, then the pronoun for il film.

activities.en: Why aren't you coming? Because I'm getting up early tomorrow.

accepted: Perché non vieni? Perché domani mi alzo presto.
activities.explanation: Perché asks and answers; io takes mi alzo.
activities.hint: Eight words, and the pronoun matches io.
Tell what someone did: who, verb, what, then when or why.
examples: Io ho mangiato la pizza ieri sera.
Noi abbiamo guardato un film dopo cena.
